sentences.text: The genus Foskeia is monotypic, containing only the species F. pelendonum, known from fossils representing several growth stages.
At roughly 0.5 m in length, Foskeia ranks among the smallest known ornithopods.
Juvenile individuals began life walking on all fours before switching to bipedal locomotion early in development.
Dieudonné and colleagues reported at least five individuals of this diminutive ornithopod in 2016.
Subsequent discovery of new cranial elements, examined with micro-CT scanning, enabled the formal naming of the genus and species in 2026.

The generic name derives from Ancient Greek words for “light” and “to forage,” reflecting its small size and presumed herbivorous diet, while the specific epithet honors the Pelendones, a Celtiberian tribe linked to the fossil locality.
Foskeia began life as a quadruped and transitioned to bipedalism during early growth, a pattern also observed in other early rhabdodontomorphs.
The largest specimen known is a late subadult, indicating that even mature individuals remained very small for ornithopods.
Foskeia is a sauropsid dinosaur belonging to the ornithischian clade Ornithopoda within the superorder Dinosauria.
In 2026 Dieudonné and colleagues assigned it to a newly defined subclade Rhabdodontia inside Rhabdodontomorpha, and described the species F. pelendonum.

Phylogenetic analyses recover Foskeia as the sister taxon to traditional Rhabdodontidae, diverging after Muttaburrasaurus and Fostoria, and place the broader rhabdodontomorph group near the base of Ankylopollexia.
Foskeia lived in the Early Cretaceous, specifically between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
Its fossils come from the Castrillo de la Reina Formation in Spain.
Researchers propose that the newly erected clade Rhabdodontia should be restricted to European rhabdodontomorphs, including Foskeia and the classic rhabdodontids.
The broader phylogenetic position of rhabdodontomorphs remains provisional, pending additional saurischian data.
